text: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up against Jerusalem to make war on it, but they could not prevail against it.

versions.text: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up against Jerusalem to make war on it, but they could not overpower it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is לְהִלָּחֵם ("to fight/wage war against"), echoing לַמִּלְחָמָה earlier in the verse. "Overpower" introduces an idea of capture not present in the wording; "prevail against" keeps the military sense and preserves the deliberate repetition, which also reads well aloud.

text: When word came to the house of David, "Aram has joined forces with Ephraim," the heart of the king and the heart of his people shook like the trees of the forest before the wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-Jashub,* at the end of the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field,

versions.text: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-Jashub, at the end of the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field,
versions.explanation: The name is symbolic and central to the chapter's message. A footnote would help the listener: *Shear-Jashub means "a remnant will return." No content change is needed to the verse itself.

text: and say to him: Be careful, keep calm, and do not be afraid. Do not lose heart over these two smoldering stubs of firewood—over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
Because Aram, together with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted evil against you, saying,
"Let us march against Judah, tear it apart, and divide it among ourselves, and set the son of Tabeel on its throne"—
this is what the Lord GOD says: It will not happen; it will not take place.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered beyond being a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in faith, you will not stand at all.
Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz:
"Ask the LORD your God for a sign—as deep as the realm of the dead or as high as the heavens."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask; I will not put the LORD to the test."
Then Isaiah said, "Listen now, house of David! Is it not enough for you to wear out human patience? Must you weary my God as well?
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: See, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she will call him Immanuel.*

versions.text: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: See, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she will call him Immanuel.
versions.explanation: The rendering is acceptable, but two footnotes would add real value for hearers: *Immanuel means "God with us"; and a note that the Hebrew word עַלְמָה may also be rendered "the young woman." The verse wording itself needs no change.

text: He will eat curds and honey by the time he knows enough to reject the wrong and choose the right.
For before the boy knows enough to reject the wrong and choose the right, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.
The LORD will bring on you and on your people and on your father's house such days as have not come since Ephraim broke away from Judah—he will bring the king of Assyria.
On that day the LORD will whistle for the flies from the distant streams of Egypt and for the bees from the land of Assyria.
They will all come and settle in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, on all the thornbushes and at all the watering holes.
On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the River—the king of Assyria—to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to take off your beard as well.
On that day a man will keep alive only a young cow and two sheep.
And because of the abundance of milk they give, he will have curds to eat. All who remain in the land will live on curds and honey.
On that day, every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver will be given over to briers and thorns.
Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the whole land will be covered with briers and thorns.
As for all the hills once cultivated with the hoe, you will no longer go there for fear of the briers and thorns; they will become places where cattle are turned loose and sheep run free.
